statements.name: Statement of financial position — NZ IFRS, Tier 2 Reduced Disclosure Regime
statements.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 Presentation of Financial Statements (with RDR disclosure concessions), paragraph 54, lists the line items a statement of financial position presents as a minimum, and paragraph 57 prescribes neither their order nor their format, so the lines below are those items in the order New Zealand practice prints them, classified current and non-current under paragraphs 60 to 76. Companies Act 1993, s. 201, and Financial Reporting Act 2013, s. 8 and s. 19 — a reporting entity that has to prepare financial statements prepares them in accordance with generally accepted accounting practice, which XRB A1 assigns to Tier 2 (NZ IFRS with reduced disclosure) for a for-profit entity that has no public accountability and elects the reduced disclosure regime. Biological assets, non-controlling interests and assets held for sale are not lines here, because the chart carries no account for them.

lines.name: Current assets
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraphs 60 to 65 — an entity presents current and non-current assets as separate classifications, an asset being current when it is expected to be realised within the operating cycle or twelve months, or is cash.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(i).

lines.name: Trade and other receivables
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(h). GST paid on purchases and the GST refund due from Inland Revenue are receivables from the Commissioner and not current tax, which paragraph 54(n) keeps for income tax; the suspense account reports here while it is in debit.

lines.name: Inventories
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(g).

lines.name: Financial assets
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(d), the part realised within twelve months.

lines.name: Current tax assets
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(n) — assets for current tax, which in New Zealand is provisional and terminal income tax, not GST: provisional tax paid, resident withholding tax deducted at source and imputation credits carried forward, and income tax refundable.

lines.name: Other current assets
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 55 — an additional line item, relevant to an understanding of the entity's financial position: prepayments and deposits paid, which are neither receivables nor financial assets.

lines.name: Non-current assets
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraphs 60 and 66 — every asset that is not current is non-current.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(a). Right-of-use assets are presented within this line, beside the assets of the same nature, which NZ IFRS 16 allows where they are disclosed in the notes; each cost account has its accumulated depreciation on the next code so that one range reaches the carrying amount.

lines.name: Investment property
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(b).

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(c).

lines.name: Investments in associates
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(e).

lines.name: Investments in joint ventures
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(e).

lines.name: Financial assets
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(d), the part not realised within twelve months.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(o) — deferred tax assets are always classified as non-current (NZ IAS 12).

lines.name: Current liabilities
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraphs 60, 69 and 70 — an entity presents current and non-current liabilities as separate classifications.

lines.name: Trade and other payables
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(k). GST collected, the GST payable to Inland Revenue, PAYE and resident withholding tax withheld are owed to the Commissioner and are not income tax, so they report here and not under paragraph 54(n); the suspense account reports here while it is in credit.

lines.name: Financial liabilities
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(m), the part due within twelve months, the credit card among them.

lines.name: Current tax liabilities
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(n) — liabilities for current tax: income tax payable and provisional tax payable.

lines.name: Provisions
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(l), the part expected to be settled within twelve months, employee leave among it.

lines.name: Non-current liabilities
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 60 — every liability that is not current is non-current.

lines.name: Financial liabilities
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(m), the part not due within twelve months.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(o).

lines.name: Provisions
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(l), the part not expected to be settled within twelve months.

lines.name: Net assets
lines.legal_reference: Not a line NZ IAS 1 lists: the subtotal a New Zealand statement of financial position prints above equity, which paragraph 55 allows. It equals total equity once the year is closed, and exceeds it by the profit of the year until then.

lines.name: Equity
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 54(r) — equity attributable to the owners of the parent; paragraph 79 asks for its classes, which are the three lines below.

lines.name: Issued capital
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 79(a) — classes of equity, such as paid-in capital.

lines.name: Reserves
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 79(b) — reserves.

lines.name: Retained earnings
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 79(b) — retained earnings, after the dividends paid that are booked beside them.

statements.name: Statement of profit or loss — NZ IFRS, Tier 2 Reduced Disclosure Regime, expenses by nature
statements.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraphs 82 and 99 to 105. Paragraph 82 lists the minimum line items — revenue, finance costs, the share of associates and joint ventures, tax expense, discontinued operations and profit or loss — and paragraph 99 requires an analysis of expenses by nature or by function, whichever is reliable and more relevant; this statement analyses them by nature, which a small company's ledger holds without any allocation. The share of the profit or loss of equity-accounted investments and discontinued operations are not lines here, because the chart carries no account for them.

lines.name: Revenue
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 82(a).

lines.name: Other income
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 85 — an additional line item: income that is not revenue from contracts with customers: interest, rent, grants, foreign exchange gains and gains on disposal.

lines.name: Raw materials, consumables and goods for resale used
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 102 — expenses analysed by their nature: purchases of materials and goods, freight inwards, import charges, the change in inventories and subcontractors.

lines.name: Employee benefits expense
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 102 — employee benefits costs, KiwiSaver employer contributions and ACC levies among them.

lines.name: Depreciation and amortisation expense
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 102 — depreciation.

lines.name: Other expenses
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 102 — the other expenses by nature, foreign exchange losses and losses on disposal among them.

lines.name: Finance costs
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 82(b).

lines.name: Income tax expense
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 82(d) — tax expense.

lines.name: Profit for the year
lines.legal_reference: NZ IAS 1 (RDR), paragraph 82(f) — profit or loss. The pack carries no item of other comprehensive income, so this is also the total comprehensive income of paragraph 82(i), which the paragraph allows to be called profit or loss.
